title: Core2-for-AWS-IoT-Kit issue 108: license compatibility with upstream cryptoauthlib

execution.environment: macOS, read-only clone (git clone --depth 50), no device service, no emulator, no build

checks.name: root and per-example license inventory
checks.detail: root LICENSE = MIT (c) 2020 Amazon Web Services; no NOTICE for third-party components; GitHub license API returns spdx_id=MIT

checks.name: vendored cryptoauthlib presence and version
checks.detail: 5 of 7 examples vendor components/esp-cryptoauthlib/cryptoauthlib at cryptoauthlib-v3.7.9; Microchip LICENSE preserved in all 5 (sha256 17f8ada09570f01b9e2c3c995f220fce01ffb61c6b8c0199f6f6ac2f355cd7d2)

checks.name: component linkage into firmware
checks.detail: Blinky-Hello-World/main/CMakeLists.txt:3 and components/core2forAWS/CMakeLists.txt:36 require esp-cryptoauthlib; atecc608.c includes cryptoauthlib.h

checks.name: pip dependency metadata for pinned version
checks.detail: cryptoauthlib==20250916 sdist sha256 c73272d66f5e2fff7835b8872e92b41d8d9f4211ebfd38db854781922efc91ad; PKG-INFO License: Other / Other/Proprietary; LICENSE.txt requires use exclusively with Microchip products

checks.name: firmware build and binary symbol verification
checks.detail: examples not compiled; linkage inferred from CMake requires and includes

checks.name: distribution channel license packaging
checks.detail: no release assets in repo; docs/M5Burner packaging not inspectable from source

notes: REVIEW only: static licensing analysis, no runtime or device validation is applicable
finding: repository-level scope disclosure gap (MIT root without third-party notice), not a copyleft-style incompatibility
Microchip redistribution clause is already satisfied at file level because each vendored copy keeps LICENSE
legal acceptability of a field-of-use restricted license left to maintainers/legal
